verdict: Starbucks revenue slipped 1% to $9.1B as comparable sales fell 3% on fewer customer visits — and higher store labor costs and promotions cut net earnings 8% to $1.1B.

segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales fell 2%, with 6% fewer transactions partly offset by a 3% higher average ticket.

footerNote: Reported operating income of $1,518M includes $74M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income. Starbucks reports in tenths of a million; this page rounds to whole millions (reported net earnings were $1,055.7M, of which $1,054.8M attributable to Starbucks).

takeaways.title: Customers came less often
takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales fell 3% as transactions dropped 5% — a 2% higher average ticket only partly offset the lost visits. North America comparable sales fell 2% and China's fell 14%.

takeaways.title: Margins squeezed by labor and deals
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin contracted 60 basis points to 16.7%: Starbucks spent more on store partner wages and benefits and ran more promotions while selling less. Store operating expenses rose 4% to $3,829M even as revenue fell.

takeaways.title: Profit slipped, stores kept opening
takeaways.text: EPS fell 6% to $0.93 and net earnings 8% to $1,056M. Starbucks still opened 526 net new stores in the quarter, ending with 39,477 — 52% company-operated and 48% licensed.
